clue.text: Drink knocked back in Colorado Springs

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is tipped up, so the run of letters is read from right to left
the letters sit inside the following place name, spanning the gap between its two words

parts.note: the tail of Colorado and the head of Springs

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink while visiting Colorado Springs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' feels like part of the drinking picture, but it is the instruction to read the hidden letters in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink, often a mixer, so it is a straightforward example of a beverage.

parts.note: a bob is an old shilling, abbreviated S; 'first' places it at the front
a sponge is slang for a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: SpongeBob, the cartoon character, catches sight of an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: SpongeBob splits in two: a sponge is a boozer, and bob is the pre-decimal shilling, written S. 'First' puts the shilling ahead of the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stippler is an artist who applies colour as small dots or dabs, so the word names a kind of painter.

parts.note: the ear, nose and throat department
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: A net sum is what a hospital department charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' reads like the money left after costs, but it is a verb meaning catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch it in a mesh, and to entrap is to catch by trickery or snare.

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the first word holds the next one inside it

parts.note: a mosaic is made by laying small tiles
RA is the Royal Academy, the body of artists, or one of its members

explanation.surface: A mosaic craftsman puts on a showing for some painters.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer is a short advance showing of clips, so it works as a preview of the coming release.

clue.text: Detective acquires basic skill after month with English novel

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so one piece ends up inside the other

parts.note: abbreviation for January
standard abbreviation
a private eye is a detective
one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A detective learns the basics after a month spent on English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' lets the detective with its added R follow the month and English, so the pieces read in the order JAN, E, EYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is the 1847 work of fiction by Charlotte Brontë, a classic English novel.

indicators.note: when something leaves it is no longer there, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a gelatine-based blasting explosive
hair gel sets a hairstyle

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler storms off, leaving a volatile scene ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' points at the compiler, but here it is hair gel; take it from the front of gelignite.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something is to set it alight, the same verb sense as kindle or set burning.

clue.text: Job for one to criticise king

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval
chess notation for king

explanation.surface: It is someone's task to find fault with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like a task, but with its capital it is the Old Testament text, and 'for one' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Job is one of the books of the Bible, so it is an instance of the wider category.

clue.text: Roll over for one at sea

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means put X in the place of Y, swapping one letter for another

parts.note: a ship rolls or lists to one side
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A ship rolls over, with one sailor lost at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical surface makes 'at sea' look literal, but it means bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for being confused and without bearings, the same as feeling lost.

indicators.note: romantic means fanciful and not true to reality, so the next word's letters are freely reimagined

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doomed priestess falls for a Roman with a passionate streak.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma is the title role of Bellini's opera: a druid priestess, in Roman-occupied Gaul, who loves the Roman proconsul and dies on the pyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's heroine is a high priestess of the druids whose story ends in self-sacrifice, making her a tragic figure.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reliable and in ... condition, as in a sound investment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' tempts a solver towards noises, but it is the adjective meaning solid and dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both for something reliable and in fine condition and for a person of upright moral character.

indicators.note: to swallow is to take inside, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: a jape is a prank, so a japer plays them
the clothing-size abbreviation

explanation.surface: A prankster gulps down a little jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque variety of quartz, often red, used as an ornamental stone in jewellery.

clue.text: In case of emergency chooses sharp tools

parts.note: the label for an emergency contact stored in a phone
to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone selects pointed implements to keep handy for a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase looks like a stock expression but supplies its own initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice picks are pointed spikes for chipping ice or climbing, so they are pointed hand implements.

clue.text: Discovered spotted dick originally eaten for dessert

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the covering taken off, so the outer letters are stripped

parts.note: dappled means marked with spots or patches
a dick is slang for a detective, a private investigator

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is caught eating spotted dick, the British steamed pudding, as dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British suet pudding with currants, which makes 'spotted dick' look like a single dish; it splits into an adjective and slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pie is a baked fruit tart served after the main course, a classic sweet course.

clue.text: Plans to involve Labour leader in revolutionary standstill

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the word runs backwards
to involve is to bring something into the middle of a thing, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a stop is a standstill

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Schemes to get the Labour Party head mixed up in a radical deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots are secret schemes or plans, and the plural noun matches the plural in the clue.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gives way or gives up, a verb
second meaning: the amounts produced, as of a crop, a plural noun

explanation.walkthrough: The two words have different parts of speech, and the answer serves as both verb and plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means gives in to force; as a noun its plural covers harvests, returns and other outputs.

parts.note: a fox lives in a den
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Fox burrows crammed with soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxholes' suggests trenches in battle, but here it is just homes of foxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dense has its matter crowded closely together, with little space between particles.

clue.text: Line in metaphor about old women

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: a trope is a figure of speech such as metaphor
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation, as on lavatory doors

explanation.surface: A line in a figure of speech refers to elderly ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' seems to be a line of text, but it is a cord or cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A towrope is a rope or cable used to haul a vehicle, and line is a general word for such a cord.

indicators.note: about can mean moved around, so these letters are scattered into a fresh order

parts.note: film-rating abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up sunk in hopelessness thinks about the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: The A joins the letters of despair before they are all rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the abode of the blessed after death, a direct synonym for the celestial afterlife.

clue.text: Gas results from cook quitting heroin substitute

indicators.note: something quitting departs, so its letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: the opioid prescribed in place of heroin
to do a dish is to cook it, as in 'do the vegetables'

explanation.surface: A chef stops using a heroin replacement, and gas is the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug-rehab surface hides a simple removal from the middle of the substitute drug's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a colourless flammable compound, the main ingredient of natural gas.

clue.text: Workers welcoming South American with tools

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the first word surrounds what follows

parts.note: farm hands or factory hands are workers
S for South and A for American
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Labourers greet a visitor from South America who brings equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a linking word but supplies a letter that joins the South American inside the workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsaws are saws worked by one hand, so they are an example of manual implements.

parts.note: a stay is a prop or brace
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A brace is fixed in position so it will not shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay put is an idiom for not moving from where one is, just as remain means continuing in place.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, so the short letter goes within the place name

parts.note: Esher is a commuter town in Surrey, south-west of London
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: the answer to 7 has spent a period living in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is BOOK, defined there as Job, and Esther is likewise a book of the Old Testament; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is one of the books of the Bible, so it fits a cross-reference whose answer is a scriptural volume.

clue.text: Group of scientists occupying shelters in woods

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so these letters sit within the next word

parts.note: huts are simple shelters
the Royal Society, Britain's national academy of sciences

explanation.surface: A research team sets up camp in cabins in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: A hurst is an old word, surviving in English place names, for a wooded hill or copse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurst is an archaic term for a grove or wooded rise, so its plural means stands of trees.

clue.text: Drills French joiner used to make toy

parts.note: to drill someone is to train them
et is French for 'and', a word that joins

explanation.surface: A French carpenter uses power tools to build a plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a woodworker, but it means a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a model railway layout played with by children and hobbyists, a classic plaything.

parts.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the second fine: fair weather is fine weather

explanation.surface: A really splendid enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'fine' looks like emphasis, but each one does a different job.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or concern, as in 'that is my business' or 'that is my affair'.

clue.text: 24 hours following member of the Addams family

definitions.text: 24 hours following member of the Addams family

parts.words: 24 hours following member of the Addams family
parts.note: surface reading: a day spent tailing one of the macabre Addams household
setter's reading: the family's daughter is named Wednesday, so the clue asks for the day that comes after her name

explanation.surface: Someone spends a whole day shadowing a character from The Addams Family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Addams daughter shares her name with a weekday; the answer is the next day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A day is a period of 24 hours, and this one directly follows the girl's namesake in the week.

indicators.note: take is read as take away, so a letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: te or ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, abbreviated T
taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention to what the editor says.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the wordplay share words: read again, 'Take note of the' means remove a T from THE, then add the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention to advice or a warning, exactly what taking note of something means.

parts.note: the FO is the Foreign Office, with the possessive S added
standard abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: A ministry advances its claim to land.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster something is to encourage its growth or development, a verb close to advance or further.

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses the letter at its front

parts.note: to peel is to strip a covering away

explanation.surface: A fishmonger cuts the heads from fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snakelike creatures that live in water, a familiar kind of fish.

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: the New Testament, a collection of books
an ex is a former partner, and ex- means former

explanation.surface: Accounts written about a clothing shop that used to trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Next is a major British high-street clothing chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Next is a UK chain selling clothes and homeware, so it is a brand that retails fashion.

clue.text: Members of mass audience from the Middle East

indicators.note: members belong to a larger body, so the letters are part of the words that follow

parts.note: the last letter of mass and the first four of audience

explanation.surface: People in a huge crowd have come from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Saudi describes things or people of Saudi Arabia, a large country on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Very possibly my hole in the ground

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in 'it may ... rain', meaning quite likely
second meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
third meaning: a shaft sunk to reach water or oil

explanation.walkthrough: 'my' looks like a possessive attached to the hole, but it is an exclamation; this is three definitions, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adverb of likelihood, as an interjection of surprise, and as a noun for a shaft dug for water.
